title: Orientational order on non-orientable domains
authors: Gianmarco Spera, Axel Fotso Ndefo, Keaton J. Burns, Alexander Mietke
abstract: We study the statistical properties of passive and active many-body systems with orientational degrees of freedom on non-orientable domains. By rephrasing topological constraints as non-local symmetry relations on an orientable double-cover, we show that non-orientability eliminates global rotational soft modes without acting like an external field. In a passive XY model, this results in topological caging, where orientational fluctuations that exhibit conventional diffusive behavior on a torus saturate on a Klein bottle to a finite value that we compute exactly in the thermodynamic limit. In models of active self-propelled particles with orientational degrees of freedom, topological caging persists despite continuously changing interaction neighborhoods. In an active Ising spin model, non-orientability enforces the coexistence of ordered anti-parallel domains with vanishing global polar order, a state that is absent on orientable domains.
summary: This work analyzes how placing orientational spin systems on non-orientable manifolds, like the Klein bottle, fundamentally changes their statistical mechanics compared to standard surfaces like the torus. The key finding is that non-orientability causes 'topological caging,' which limits orientational fluctuations to a finite value, a robust effect seen in both passive and active matter models.
main_problem: The study investigates how the non-orientable topology of a domain, specifically the Klein bottle, alters the statistical properties and orientational fluctuations of many-body systems compared to standard orientable domains like the torus.
main_result: Non-orientability eliminates global rotational soft modes and induces 'topological caging' in passive systems, leading to finite saturation of orientational fluctuations, a state absent on the torus.
method: The authors employ stochastic microscopic equations, mean-field theory, and spin-wave approximations, analyzing the system's dynamics by mapping topological constraints onto non-local symmetry relations on an orientable double-cover.
model_or_system: The models include the passive XY spin model and active self-propelled particle systems (like the active Ising model) whose orientations are constrained on a Klein bottle geometry, contrasting with the torus geometry.
key_observables: Global orientation fluctuation $\langle\delta\Theta^2(t)angle$, polar order parameter $|M|$, and the spin polarization distribution $P(m_x, m_y)$.
important_parameters: The comparison between the torus and Klein bottle topologies, and the role of the non-local symmetry relations imposed by non-orientability.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on the spin-wave approximation for small angle variations and the mathematical mapping of topological constraints to symmetry relations on a double-cover.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the double-cover representation of the Klein bottle and compare the time evolution of orientation fluctuations ($\langle\delta\Phi^2angle$) on both the torus and the Klein bottle, showing saturation on the latter.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the topological constraints via the double-cover, then analyzing the dynamics of passive XY models to show topological caging, and finally extending these findings to active particle models like the active Ising spin model.
why_interesting: The concept of topological constraints fundamentally altering equilibrium dynamics (caging) without requiring an explicit external field is a rich theoretical topic relevant to understanding complex phase behavior in condensed matter systems.
